The player is Ansel Mott.

Lying here, and takeable: nothing.

The player is carrying: pawn ticket, brass tally (picked up just now, on this turn).

What just happened: You stand at the pawnbroker's counter with your ticket in hand. Tamsin and Rowe are both behind it.

What has ALREADY happened, recorded by the game: ON THIS TURN, and not before it, Ansel Mott picked the brass tally up. The picking up is what has just happened and it is what to narrate. Do not write it as something they already had, already held, or turn out to be holding. The brass tally is the only thing that moved: nothing else was lifted, opened, drawn out or taken into anybody's hands.
Narrate it as done. Do not contradict it and do not undo it.
